title: The evidence file a chatbot cannot assemble
blurb: Most readers evaluating an idea already pay for a frontier chatbot, and IDEA_ANALYSIS §5 says the honest response is to feed it rather than compete with it. A finished report now hands its whole self over as Markdown — every claim with the verbatim span it came from, every source with a URL and a date. Rendered in Rust rather than in the browser, because the page already draws this data and a second renderer would hold a second opinion about what a source’s standing is called. Quotes lose their line breaks and nothing else; the size bound names the sections it dropped rather than stopping halfway. Running it against a real company found what no test would have: the provenance line was printing the inference server’s address, in the one document written to be pasted into somebody else’s service.
